Beautifully created scenery, but above all else, absolutely killer voice acting and writing. Basically the only reason, and its a good reason, to play this game is for the characters. The gameplay itself is pretty meh...walk here, turn dial to this or that, talk to people...yeah that's actually pretty much it. But its short and sweet and just so damn lovable. Worth the few hours it takes to play and maybe even another few replays just for kicks since it has that feature built in as part of the story even. It does make you wonder at the end, what would happen if I did things differently? Always a great quality in a game.
Nice little game with a bunch of different endings. Good if you want something that is goal oriented. Wish there was more gameplay and less running around though:)

Nice game. Maybe a bit too short for the full price, but it's been bundled a couple of times so you can get it almost for free.

No really much to say about this one, if not for the fact that it would have been nice to have some indications about HOW you are going to say something. I mean like adding a or after the phrases. A lot of times what you are going to say after chosing an option can't be inferred by the option itself. Like you choose "Yeah" because you want to agree with something, and Alex says "Yeah, sure, whatever, I don't care" while sounding pissed off. In the end it doesn't matter much, but it didn't make me feel much in control sometimes.

Honestly, this light horror game was a great game with a rich, well-told, remarkable, but yet a bit dramatic story. Love the painting/watercolored type of graphics, everything looks beautiful. Loved the dialogues which were quite entertaining espacially when they can influence the ending you get. Reminds me a bit of Until Dawn (PS4), but less scary of course. Don't think it worths 22$ CAD though. The only real issue for me is the slow gameplay, it takes you 6 hours to complete a 3 hours game. Characters walk really slowly and dialogues are long sometimes. I will recommand to get it on sale. This is a good 7/10 for me.

There is nothing better then a good story game that has a mysterious ambience to it when you are alone a friday evening. If you are looking for that kind of game, Oxenfree is right up you're ally!

11/10

This game is totally awesome !

I've but only two complaints :

I won't talk much about the scenario because I myself didn't know what the game would be about, (I bought it long before playing it)and found that it's so much better to discover it on your own.
Just know that this game is a little indie gem that was taking dust in my library, and I'm totally glad I finally played it.

An incredibly interesting concept, this game has some of the most fluid and natural dialogue I've ever seen in a game. It's not just that the voice acting is perfect, which it is, but that the things the characters say truly sound like how people normally talk. That might seem like a small thing, but in a game based heavily around dialogue it's a real blessing. The story is incredible, the mystery is very engaging, and parts will have your heart in your throat. Bonus points for an incredibly chill soundtrack, and for all the interesting little snippets you hear on the various radio channels, especially all the old Bugs Bunny bits

Oxenfree is a very atmospheric game with great music and beautifully crafted backgrounds. The characters and their relationships with each other are also well written; they feel real and genuine, and you as the player are in charge where they will go. Your (dialogue) choices affect on will you become/stay friends with them. Basically, you can be nice or mean, or silent the entire game.
Oxenfree may not be listed as a horror game, and I wouldn't really call it one. But it has some elements of horror to spice the game up. There also are a couple jump scares, but for once they don't bother me. One part I found very intriguing in this game is the camera. The entire game is from the same angle, but the camera has a subtle movement what makes it feel like you, the player, are stalking the characters through the night.

Few downsides in Oxenfree are that your choices mainly are only dialogue options. You will be presented with a couple non-dialogue related choices, but it's not really a lot. It didn't bother me but I still want to get it out there. Also, where the music and backgrounds are beautiful, the character models seem a bit off. I don't think they are very bad, but they could be better too.

Regardless, I warmheartedly recommended getting this game.

A great interactive story, if a little short. I'm not sure there are "puzzles" per se, or if there is a challenge in this game. It's more about the atmosphere and the the whole feeling of wholesomeness this piece of art is offering. Highly recommended.

A very atmospheric adventure game with simple gameplay.
Pros

Great, suspenseful atmosphere
Often great dialogues
Beautiful music and haunting sound effects

Cons

Simple, monotonous gameplay
The writing can be uneven (but maybe that's how the specific teens really talk)

I recommend Oxenfree but bear in mind that the gameplay is very simple. It's pretty much a 2D walking+talking simulator, as walking and talking constitute 99% of what you'll be doing.

Neat little game, reminds me of the walking dead games but way more depth of choice. Also looks beautiful and the musics and atmosphere in general are great. The puzzles are not super complicated, never gets frustrating but not particularly challenging either. 4 hours to finish so that's also a plus that it doesn't last forever.

This is, without a doubt, the best 'interactive story' game I played since the first season of TWD. And the story itself isn't even that interesting. What's really wothy is how conversations feel in a mechanical way. Just to talk is actually enjoyable here. The devs made a great job to make this chats feel natural. And the solution was so simple that I don't understand how more devs didn't try this before. It all basically summs to a simple, but intelligent control scheme design (I recommend to play the game with a controller), where you have a unique and dedicated button for every type of answer. This design let all the chats occur in gameplay, and this lets you enjoy the experience without that weird disconnection that happens with the game mode changes (walk mode/chat mode) that occur in basically all the current releases of the genre. As I said above, maybe its major flaw is it's plot. Don't get me wrong. It's nicely written and acted, but is too 'adolescent' for my taste. Anyway, mechanically speaking, this is a great step for the genre, and I hope more devs will take notes of what this game did with its conversation system, so we can enjoy more -and more varied- great feeling story driven games like Oxenfree.

it's a good game with a good story and good soundtrack and of course good atmosphere
but sometimes the dialogue especially how the character should react toward an event that "scary" is missplace
overall i recommend this game....

Great story and soundtrack. The dialogues are the best, especially the excellent voice acting. You have to listen actively and always choose quickly from the 3 decisions in the dialogues. There is a kind of karma system for all characters. By making certain decisions, you can upset characters and their moods towards other characters. This can also lead to an argument. Other serious decisions that change the entire course of the story must also be made regularly. But I don't want to spoil anything. If you don't know what to do on a boring evening, just play this game. Its like a 4-5 hour interactive film.

Oxenfree is a story game, the meat and potatoes so to speak is the dialogue, characters and overall story.
The story is really intriguing and I think the characters are very charming. Highlights being Alex and Jonas and their new relationship as step-brother and sister.
However since the story is fairly short I am going to refrain from saying too much about it since I really recommend that you check it out yourself and experience it.

For the other stuff the music in particular is fenomenal and I listen to it from time to time just because of how good it is.

There really isn't much more to say to be honest, it's a short game, it's very cheap to buy and it's an easy recommendation from me!

I'm about half way through, loving it. I can tell I'm going to play it again to try some of the other options. I like the lead character and her step-brother. I like how you can tell when the characters are forming opinions about each other. I -really- want to know what happened to the brother, and I'll bet I'm going to find out. Next play-through, I'll probably use a walkthrough, but this time I'm playing just on my own, and loving it.
with a hidden mystery on a small abandoned island and a group of stupid teens you fight against monsters with a radio

I did not expect to enjoy this game so much, and if became one of my favorites I ever played. I played it *several* times, over and over again, just to try and get all the endings. Great story, dug the graphics the soundtrack. The puzzles are simple, but the way they intringingly mesh with the story makes, you not even care. This is one of those games where choices matter, and character development goes every which way depending on how you act.

The only con I can think of is that you want more after its all over and you will search in vain for finding anything else like it.
I love this game and the amount of details put into each choice, it makes it feel like there's infinite endings.
A good game with an interesting way to tell story and present dialogues, great music, and a lot of bad design decisions. Like the saving mechanic is pretty stupid.
Very good game. Graphics are good. Story is unique, if you like stranger things just play it. Easily 2-3 playthroughs.
Definitely a great game with vibes of Life is Strange, and Tell Tale games, where your choices matter. It also features beautiful artwork, and chill electronic music.

A four hour game with some of the best art, music, sound design, and character interaction I've played in a while. The controls are super simple and there's no way to really 'lose' in any moment. Be aware that there are some light jumpscares throughout, but this is definitely NOT a horror game.

I'm gonna go buy an old radio.

An unsettling point and click, pick your own "adventure," (more like dialogue) coming of age story. There are multiple endings that really open the story up. New Game + lets you play the main story line again, but this time it changes some of the dialogue which cements some more of the creepy aspects of the plot. At times the controls can be a little tedious and the pacing a little slow, but overall I would recommend for even just the music alone.

I really wanted to like this game but after playing it for an hour I had to put it down. I found the controls to be lacking along with the bland menus and aggravating interface. Side by side with the controls I thought the Dialogue options faded away extremely fast and there's just not enough of it. You spend way too much time just walking and once you're no longer concerned by the story's ambiguous nature it begins to feel like a chore. it's wasn't an enjoyable game for me.

If it was a TV Show, I'd be all over it. Podcast, it'd be my go to while jogging or even if it was made into a comic. I understand the appell and I see why people liked it, unfortunately, I didn't.

This is a nice little game thats mostly story and dialogue driven. It is essentially a walking simulator with some very minor puzzle elements. Mostly the "gameplay" consists of choosing dialogue options and stearing conversations.

That being said if you dont expect a point and click adventure you get a few hours of a rather interesting story with very well written and believable dialogue and likable characters. Dialogue choices offer some replay value and there are some differences in the endings but overal since most of the fun in this game (the mystery) is gone after the first playthrough the replay value isnt that high. Thats also why I would say that without a sale the price is a littles steep.

Still pick it up on a sale and play though it on a weekend afternoon and it will probably keep you well entertained for its duration.

There are two major flaws that prevented me from getting far at all and make me not recommend this game. One, as mentioned by some others, the dialogue system is flawed in that the choices disappear so fast, you have to cut off everyone as they are speaking. I would prefer a slight pause for me to choose something because it feels downright jarring and ruins the flow of conversations. Entire dailogues will get skipped or interrupted for some offhand comment by your character that doesn't matter. Second, for a game based so heavily around dialogue, it is god awful. I don't know if the creator has ever interacted with humans before, but half of the things said make it seem like every character has aspergers. It is a shame because the art is great and the game has great potential otherwise.

The gameplay is very much point and click but the story is very engaging. Have not found another game that feels like this and the visuals have their own feel to them. this is a very unique game that is worth a visit. I also love the horror elements added to the story which is a mystery that you and the group of friends try to uncover as the game unfolds.

A magnificent dialogue-driven narrative experience.

Oxenfree is an adventure game that follows the school of Telltale's decision-based interactive stories. Beyond its unassuming appearance as a teenage adventure, you'll find a quality horror tale that touches upon existential notions and throws some very hard choices at the player.

The backgrounds are absolutely spectacular to look at and the atmosphere is incredible. There are no puzzles to speak of, but the game features a radio that the main character uses to tune into different frequencies, which the player can use to interact with the world and discover secrets. It's a central mechanic and it works into creating the unique atmosphere of the game at multiple levels that would be a shame for me to spoil. Suffice to say, it's very, very unique.

To anyone who appreciates Telltale games and the entire subset of fantastic games they inspired, Oxenfree is an absolute must.

Why is this Deck Verified? For one thing, crossplatform (between Deck and Windows 10) Cloud Saves are not working on Main branch or on Beta branch. For another thing, not as important or game breaking--Deck in portable mode is offering resolutions larger than Native, in-game.

The dialogue system is extremely wonky. Characters will interrupt each other and themselves if environmental tooltips are activated during a dialogue conversation. Either grey out tooltips until convos are over or implement an improved dialogue system to handle queue-ing better.

I personally need more seconds to decide which dialogue I want to select. Game also kinda suffers from Fallout 4's problem of vague/undesired dialogue/attitude based on misleading/incomplete dialogue selection previews/summaries.

The atmosphere and plot seems very intriguing thus far though. Super creepy and unsettling.

Even though I love the music and sound design, like other reviewers I did notice the disappointing absence of a music volume slider, or volume sliders in general. Actually, many settings are missing or underwhelming. I would also appreciate a Gamma slider in Display/Graphics settings.

Don't touch that FM/AM transponder, stay tuned!

Oxenfree is a very good looking game and the art style is interesting, but a good interesting. The soundtrack adds to the whole experience, and makes me feel like im watching a movie. This game has the ability to make me amazed and freaked out at the same time, due to the plot and the music and sounds throughout the game. The multiple endings are a nice add also, making it so your choices actually matter.

The only problem I have with this game is that the speech options fade away so fast and I can't always say something without interrupting the person speaking, which kind of annoyed me. Overall, I recommend this game if you are into exploration or story-rich games.
This game has a really intriguing story and amazing gameplay. If you like games like Life is Strange or Until Dawn I really think you will enjoy this game as well as it's story. Highly recommend!

Such a beautiful game artisticly and story wise. Yes iv'e read that its a pretty slow game(though it took me 6 hours to beat and that's including all the *secrets*) and yes it is at some slower parts like why do we need 50 switchbacks! but that's because of the story focus, in other words the game play is about interacting and growing to know the characters better and deciding the relationship you are gonna have with them. If this kind of game (adventure, light puzzels, mostly exploration and character based) you sometimes play, play this one. The mysteries are interesting. I am a gamer at heart and have played many games. This game is a nice game to sit back and enjoy the click through. The changes between the first play though and the second where subtle but yet amazing when i started to notice them.
There is only one thing I would change. Please make this a change If you are a Dev for OxenFree II. Give me the ability to Mute the sound track. I tried to play through while streaming on Twitch and parts of my stream was muted due to Copyrighted music.

The game is pretty short, but it really is a lot of fun! Beautiful soundtrack, interesting characters, and the story is pretty entertaining from star to finish! At first I wasn't entirely sure I'd like the game too much, but for what it's worth, I highly recomend it!

Play the game dammit it's definitely worth it!

My roommate and I have both gone about reccing this game to anyone we meet and I'm here to do the same. tl;dr PLAY IT

Eerie island vibes, razor-sharp dialogue choices, and radio-hacking puzzles. Short, stylish, and unforgettable supernatural thriller. 9/10.
Boy, did I like it.
Game looks like a lot of fun, but holly fu*k the music is so goddamn loud and obnoxious...how can you make a game and not add volume in the settings is baffling.

I like the characters, the mystery, the conversation mechanic. I don't like retreading on the big island and the people walking through it slowly. The game has value in replay, but its not incredibly fun because takes so long to replay and the gameplay itself was so boring to me on the second playthrough that I didn't go through with a third to get the ending I wanted. When there were different plot events it was really interesting. Hopefully they fixed up some of this on the second game. Someone said "the developers want you to feel stuck." I don't know if that's true but if so I guess they succeeded? I overall recommend the game, because I'm glad I played it, but I wish there was a middle option to say I only kind of recommend it, or feel mixed about it.

It's cheap so I didn't expect to much but, honestly after playing for 5 hours and completing it (I think), I didn't rate it at all. I was expecting a point and click style adventure with lots of puzzles and for it to get progressively harder. It doesn't get harder at all. It's practically a story book which you read, click a few places and the story is told to you. The puzzles are so easy it could be done by a toddler. I'd say the storyline is aimed at young teenage girls, but it promotes smoking, drinking, sex (in one part) and there's suicide and death involved. So, really, it's a kids game, but is not obviously aimed at kids. Don't waste your time or money, unless you feel like enjoying a gossip based teen drama which was somehow developed in to a game.

I bought this game (partly) because I read it's worth playing twice, and choices matter. I only played it once, but I'm almost sure that you can't drastically change the main storyline. Maybe I would find some easter eggs for the second try, but I don't feel like there's enough content for a second run. Maybe I'm wrong :) However it's still a great game for so many reasons.

Pro:
- Wonderfull dialogs, continous talking and real time choices really make you want to be part of the conversation and not just choose the best option and skip to the goal.
- Awesome characters with detailed moral and background story.
- The idea of the radios is really cool. Perfect retro sci-fi. The tuning minigame is quiet simple, but I think the story is more important.
- Beautiful artwork and mood.

Con:
- It's a generic ghost story with a lot of cliches. I wish it was more sci-fi.
- It's still not clear what the bubbles with the heads represent. It's not a clear feedback.
- Your choices matter, but not too much :/

It's way better than I expected, the story is good and interesting, characters are deep. The only issue is the pacing. Sometimes you have to walk really long distances at a really slow, but maybe that's just me.
Also, it sucks that when there's a conversation and you interact with anything, the conversation just cuts off.
